items.label: About
items.text: Hey! I'm Adrian, a 3rd year Computer Engineering student at UofT interested in graphics…

items.label: Projects
items.text: RATH - Vulkan Rendering Engine (Jun 2026 - Present): A game engine I am currently building in C++ with Vulkan. So far, I have implemented the basics of Vulkan (swapchain, renderpasses, graphics/compute pipelines, and command buffer syncs). A glTF model loader, asset manager, free-fly camera, and diffuse lighting shaders have also been added. This is all controllable in run-time through an ImGui menu.

items.label: Projects
items.text: OpenGL Shader Renderer (May 2026 - Aug 2026): A multi-pass deferred C++/OpenGL renderer with three non-photorealistic GLSL shaders: cel shading (inspired by Guilty Gear Xrd), crosshatch/screentone, and isophote contours. Features two-tone cel lighting, rim lighting, screen-space outlines from normal and depth buffers, and a ping-pong Gaussian bloom pipeline with HDR tone mapping.

items.label: Projects
items.text: GANTerrainGen (May 2026 - Jul 2026): A DCGAN trained on satellite data (Copernicus elevation + ESA WorldCover) to procedurally generate 256x256 terrain maps, benchmarked against a Perlin fBm baseline. Created as my APS360 final project. Build a real-time C++/OpenGL visualizer to inspect training checkpoints live.

name: Evan Lin
talking_points: Ask how a group of students with no hardware background built Tiny-TPU and got it to ~1.4k stars, and what training on it taught them.
He went from Groq's distributed systems team to NVIDIA; ask what he works on and how Tiny-TPU helped him get there.
Ask about his Attention Residuals post, which compares the idea to a KV cache turned 'depth-wise' across layers.
Tiny-TPU hit the Hacker News front page in Aug 2025 and has ~1.4k stars: ask how the team split the systolic array and backprop work
Co-built TinyTPU, an open-source TPU re-invented from scratch with Surya Sure, Kenny Guo and Xander Chin; repo tiny-tpu-old has ~200 stars and the team met the inventor of the TPU
Experience at NVIDIA; studying at Western University; based in Toronto
Also built LPU Lite (lpulite.com), a Groq LPU re-invented from first principles to run Karpathy's MicroGPT, with Michael Trbovic and Arjun Harinath
NVIDIA (LinkedIn headline); studied at Western University
Built tiny-tpu, a minimal TPU-inspired chip in SystemVerilog (206 stars on GitHub)
Wrote about building attention residuals from scratch (April 2026)
Works with NVIDIA
Studies at Western University (2023 - 2027)
Award: “KSNW”, Oct 2026
About: more about my interests and writing: evanlin.ca

items.label: Recent linkedin posts
items.text: I'm excited to share that I'll be joining Y Combinator's Winter 2027 batch to build Tesser (YC W27) with Rohan Godha! Tesser lets you run multiple worktrees in parallel by offloading dev servers and other heavy workloads to isolated cloud VMs. We handle networking and port forwarding so you or a teammate can interact with any server locally. Compatible with any agentic coding setup you may have, cloud or local :) We're expanding our private beta, request early access at tesser(.)sh

items.label: Recent linkedin posts
items.text: Sold another side project! A few months ago, I joined Rohan Godha to build brainrot(.)mov, a tool to generate short form videos with Peter & Stewie Griffin voiceovers. Rohan used this to scale his instagram aws_peter to 70k+ followers, with our other users growing to 100k+ followers. We grew to a peak of $1k MRR in a few months (with no marketing except one reel). After learning all we wanted to learn from the project, we decided it was time to let it go and work on bigger things. Onwards!

name: Jerry
talking_points: He founded Akatos to make Waterloo 'heaven for makers': ask who lives there and what they're building.
He talked on the loopfour podcast about AI agents for internal workflows: ask which Unrepped workflows are fully automated.
Unrepped went through Vercel's AI Accelerator in 2025: ask how it guides buyers who purchase without an agent.
He's been promoting a Feb 2027 Waterloo physical-AI hackathon ('How to Train Your Robot'): ask what hardware builders there need.
Works with Akatos
Studies at Babson College (2011 - 2015)
About: Turning Waterloo, Canada into heaven for makers everywhere.
Posted on LinkedIn (2026-10-29): Congrats to Jackie Yi, a Waterloo fellow!

items.text: Proud to have earned the endorsement of Waterloo Region Labour Council (WRLC) for Mayor of Waterloo! The WRLC represents 33 unions and ~26,000 workers in Waterloo Region, in both public and private sectors. The election for the next Waterloo mayor is happening tomorrow (Monday) - if you see this, please go out and vote!

items.text: I'm running for Mayor of Waterloo, because this city deserves a leader who understands Waterloo's place in Canada, and the opportunities available to be seized. Voting takes place on Monday, Oct 26 - make sure to come vote! If you're a Waterloo, Laurier, or Conestoga student, you are likely eligible to vote in Waterloo! Go to canivote.ca - an app that I built myself to check if you're eligible.

items.label: About
items.text: Hi! I’m Mrida, a CS student in my third year at Western University, passionate about cybersecurity, data analysis, backend development, and building tech solutions that make a difference. My university journey has been a mix of everything, hands-on learning, and leadership, from mentoring first-year students as an Off-Campus Soph, to developing AI-powered tools like LLM-based misinformation checkers and interactive web apps such as MoodMates and Recipe Finder. I’ve gained experience in Python, Java, SQL, PowerBI, full-stack development, APIs, and modular system design, all while learning how to manage projects, collaborate with teammates, and translate complex ideas into practical solutions. Outside of university, I love to swim or experiment with new recipes! If any of this interests you feel free to reach out and connect.

items.text: We won LA Hacks. Our team built Edith, a real-time AI assistant that runs on Meta Ray-Ban glasses. You speak naturally, the glasses see what you see, and Edith handles the rest, looking up who you just met, sending follow-up emails, booking reservations, all without touching your phone. Built on Fetch.ai's OmegaClaw reasoning system and ASI Agentverse, Edith is not a voice interface. It is a fully agentic pipeline that interprets intent, delegates to specialized agents, and executes actions end

items.text: We built Vit. Version control for DaVinci Resolve. Git, but for video editors. Professional video production is broken. Editors, colorists, and sound designers work sequentially. One person finishes, hands off, and waits. Software developers solved this 30 years ago with Git. Video editors have nothing. So we fixed it. vit serializes your DaVinci Resolve timeline into domain-split JSON files. Each role owns a different file: Editor → cuts.json Colorist → color.json Sound designer → audio.json Ev

name: Sarina Cheng
school: Computer Science (BSc, Western) + HBA (Ivey Business School)
talking_points: Ask how AirClick's cross-laptop copy-paste gesture worked; it won Best Hardware Hack at SheHacks+ 10 with Brianna Xiao, who is also at HW13.
She runs Ivey Product Society and her team won its 2026 Product Case Competition; swap notes on PM recruiting from Ivey for Summer 2027.
